entries.title: MLB considering playing a game at Grand Teton National Park
entries.summary: <p>Major League Baseball has reached out to the federal government about the possibility of one day staging a game in western Wyoming's Grand Teton National Park, an idea quickly met with resistance from environmental groups and others.</p><p>MLB and the players' association have played a handful of regular-season games away from the 30 big league ballparks in recent years, including in the Iowa corn fields made famous by the movie "Field of Dreams."</p><p>An MLB official familiar with the discussions confirmed Monday that the league approached the Trump administration about possibly hosting a game in a national park. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because the league hadn't authorized comment on the matter and said it was among several ideas MLB has explored.</p><p>A White House official said MLB asked the administration whether hosting a game at a national park would be possible but emphasized it was not a presidential directive and was not driven by the administration. The National Park Service has not granted any permits, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because there was no authorization to speak on the record.</p><p>MLB's special event games have included games at Dyersville, Iowa, in 2021, 2022 and 2026, with another scheduled next August between Boston and Kansas City.</p><p>In addition, regular-season games were played at Rickwood Field in Birmingham, Alabama, in 2024 and at Bristol Motor Speedway in Bristol, Tennessee, in 2025, and games have been held since 2017 in conjunction with the Little League World Series in Williamsport, Pennsylvania.</p><p>MLB also has played international games in London; Mexico City and Monterrey, Mexico; Seoul, South Korea; Sydney; and Tokyo; plus some in San Juan, Puerto Rico.</p><p>Grand Teton includes a commercial airport — the busiest in Wyoming — and a vast expanse of Jackson Hole bottomlands with spectacular views of the Teton Range. There is no shortage of flat terrain where a temporary ballpark could be built.</p><p>The possibility of building a baseball field on national park land quickly raised a host of questions.</p><p>"It's abhorrent," Mike Gierau, a Democratic state senator and baseball lover who represents Jackson and nearby Grand Teton, wrote in a text message. "Baseball is the American game. The national parks are America's greatest idea. But a national park is to be protected for its undeveloped and scenic values."</p><p>Environmental groups also came out against the idea, first reported by The Washington Post.</p><p>"Americans want to see protections for our national parks and public lands strengthened. Bulldozing these lands for a baseball stadium does the opposite, destroying the magnificent landscapes that millions of people come to experience," Chris Kassar, the group's Wyoming director, said in a statement.</p><p>A message left with Grand Teton officials seeking more information wasn't immediately returned.<br></p>

entries.title: Hagen Smith will open up a White Sox bullpen game in Game 1 of Wild Card series against Astros
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON – Two years after being their fifth overall pick, rookie left-hander <b>Hagen Smith</b> will start the first White Sox playoff game in five years. Just like they planned, right?</p><p>Well, there’s some nuance.</p><p>Smith has been <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/24/white-sox-hagen-smith-brian-bannister-will-venable-2024-draft-jac-caglianone-konnor-griffin-trey-yesavage-pitching-development-pete-crow-armstrong" target="_blank" ><u>working as a reliever since being called up in August</u></a>, three innings represents the longest outing of his career and he won’t be improving upon it in Tuesday’s Game 1 against the Astros. Manager <b>Will Venable</b> said the Sox are throwing a bullpen game–as are the Astros, started by right-hander <b>A.J. Blubaugh</b>.</p><p>Even their oft-used strategy of an opener setting up a bulk pitcher who works four-to-five innings is more conservative than what the White Sox have planned.</p><p>“You might have a starter, a young starter, go four, five innings, perhaps even more than that,” said general manager <b>Chris Getz</b>. “But if we can get higher end two, three-inning outings from some of these guys, we're going to lean in that direction.”</p><p><b>Sean Burke </b>and <b>David Sandlin </b>split the only two starts of six innings or longer that the Sox had in all of September. The club used an opener or bullpen game an MLB-leading 31 times in 2026, and have primed their pitching staff for a relay race of one-to-three-inning appearances that will define their Wild Card series strategy.</p><p>“Kind of being doing it all year, right?” Sox pitching coach <b>Zach</b> <b>Bove</b> told the Sun-Times. “The message to all the guys is to be ready for multiple situations. That’s it. We’ll communicate as best we can to where they’re going to be. But at the same time, it’s maybe not going to be the traditional way of going about it.”</p><p>In a best-of-three series where the risk of the bullpen wearing down is lessened, the White Sox see it as a means to an end. They don’t think their fans, nor 90-year-old chairman <b>Jerry Reinsdorf </b>will fret too much about the aesthetics.</p><p>“Not if it helps us win games,” retorted Getz.</p><p><b>The likely AL MVP plays for the other side</b></p><p>Tapping Smith, when he’s held left-handed hitters to a .194/.256/.278 batting line this season, smacks of a pitching strategy built around unfavorable matchups for Astros slugger <b>Yordan Alvarez</b>, who led the American League in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601) this season.</p><p>“As great as Yordan is, he's not the only really good hitter in their lineup, so you can't just totally say, ‘Hey, we're not going to let Yordan beat us,’ and walk him every time,” said Venable.</p><p>Except the Sox kinda have. Alvarez went 4-for-20 with a double against the Sox this year, but he scored five runs in seven games because they walked him at a 27.6% clip. If avoiding Alvarez doesn’t work, a bullpen game could ensure he faces a left-hander almost every time.</p><p>“He hasn't really kind of hurt us, so we feel generally good about the plan,” Bove said. “But obviously he is a great hitter.”</p><p><b>Meidroth should be good to go</b></p><p>After not playing in the final series–outside of a pinch-hit double on Saturday–due to a sore left hamstring, second baseman<b> Chase Meidroth</b> is expected to be able to play on Tuesday.</p><p>“He's going to be maybe not 100%, but as close to a normal version of Chase as we can get right now,” Venable said.</p>

entries.title: A look at the top contenders for the Sun-Times high school football player of the year
entries.summary: <p>Kameron McGee caught a screen pass from Sam Holcomb in the third quarter of Brother Rice’s win against Mount Carmel in Week 6.</p><p>The junior defensive superstar beat two defenders, then raced past three more for a 33-yard touchdown that gave the Crusaders the lead for good.</p><p>It was an eye-opening moment that showed how much the exceptional athlete could impact every phase of the game. It was a Player of the Year-caliber moment.</p><p>McGee is one of the best college prospects in the country, the best junior prospect in the nation according to some evaluators, and has been on the POY radar since the preseason.</p><p>Brother Rice’s win against the Caravan and McGee’s starring role certainly helped his case. McGee also had four tackles, four hurries, a sack and a TFL in the game.</p><p>Lincoln-Way East quarterback Jonas Williams was an easy pick for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2025/12/17/jonas-williams-chicago-sun-times-player-of-the-year-lincoln-way-east-usc" >Sun-Times Player of the Year</a> last season. Williams set state records for career passing yards and career TD passes.</p><p>No player this year has that level of historic resume, but it is an uncommonly strong year overall, with multiple excellent contenders after six weeks.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Kam McGee also scores touchdowns. Brother Rice’s defensive star catches a pass from Sam Holcomb, sheds tacklers and scores a 33-yard TD. <br><br>What a game. The Crusaders lead Mount Carmel 28-24 in the 3Q. <a href="https://t.co/rUdF9KWNpb">pic.twitter.com/rUdF9KWNpb</a></p>— Michael O'Brien (@michaelsobrien) <a href="https://x.com/michaelsobrien/status/2103663569376051507?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>McGee is certainly in the race. Here’s a look at some other top contenders.</p><h3>Israel Abrams, Montini</h3><p>The senior quarterback is carrying a huge load for the Broncos. Abrams, a Miami recruit, threw for 411 yards against Nazareth and 398 yards in the Week 6 loss to St. Rita. He’s thrown 18 touchdown passes so far this season.</p><p>Abrams will finish the season with POY numbers, and his put together a career very worthy of the award. Another state title run will be a key factor in Abrams’ candidacy.</p><h3>Jake Thies, Fenwick</h3><p>The Iowa recruit is the best full-time two-way player in the area. Thies, the breakout star of last season’s football state finals, is lighting up the stat sheet as a running back and defensive back. He has 65 carries for 574 yards and 18 catches for 255 yards with nine total touchdowns. Defensively, he’s added 56 tackles, 5 TFLs, and an interception.</p><p>The Friars were ranked for about half the season. Team success will play a major factor in Thies’s POY chances. Fenwick has big regular-season games remaining against Providence and Carmel, so Thies has two major opportunities to sparkle before the playoffs even begin.</p><h3>Jake Nawrot, Hersey</h3><p>The Huskies didn’t play a Week 6 game because Wheeling forfeited, so Nawrot’s stats cover just five games. The Kentucky recruit is 87-for-127, throwing for 1,321 yards, 17 touchdowns, and no interceptions.</p><p>Hersey’s final regular-season game against Prospect will be a major opportunity for Nawrot to open more eyes. A very deep run in the Class 7A playoffs will be key for Nawrot’s POY chances.</p><h3>Ben Peterson and Bennett Konkey, Geneva</h3><p>The two biggest surprises on the list. Peterson, an Eastern Michigan recruit, has thrown for 1,847 yards and 22 TDs with just two interceptions this season. Bennett Konkey, Peterson’s top receiver, is also a major POY candidate. The Illinois recruit has 46 catches for 961 yards and 13 TDs this season. The Vikings’ Week 6 win against Batavia was a major resume booster for both players.</p><h3>Michael Vander Luitgaren, Batavia</h3><p>The numbers are huge for Vander Luitgaren, a Wyoming recruit. He’s 126-for-164 passing for 1,801 yards and 23 TDs with five interceptions. He’s also rushed for nine touchdowns. Batavia has a major win against Maine South, but Vander Luitgaren will likely need a Class 7A state title to win POY, especially after the loss to Geneva.</p><p><b>Other contenders to watch include Mount Carmel receiver Marshaun Thornton, Maine South quarterback Jameson Purcell, and Loyola linebacker Will Mettee.</b></p>
